Shawn Van Horn is a Senior Author for Collider. He's watched way too many slasher movies over the decades, which makes him an aficionado on all things Halloween and Friday the 13th. Don't ask him to choose between Michael Myers and Jason Voorhees because he can't do it. He grew up in the 90s, when Seinfeld, Everybody Loves Raymond, and TGIF were his life, and still watches them religiously to this day. Larry David is his spirit animal. His love for entertainment spreads to the written word as well. He has written two novels and is neck deep in the querying trenches. He is also a short story maker upper and poet with a dozen publishing credits to his name. He lives in small town Ohio, where he likes to watch professional wrestling and movies.

There is no newspaper comic strip more famous than Charles M. Schulz's Peanuts. Running for a whopping 50 years, the strip followed the adventures of Charlie Brown and company as they moved through life and its seasons. Among them are the meanings found in Thanksgiving and Christmas, including some famous TV specials. Then there's how Peanuts approached Halloween.

From Charlie Brown's observations to the hijinks of his dog Snoopy, the spookiest time of the year provided a lot of material for the comic. While Peanuts in Autumn is most well known for Linus's belief in the Great Pumpkin, especially in It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown, many of Peanuts' best Halloween moments happened in the pages of the daily newspaper.

7
"That's the Best Treat Lucy Will Get All Night"

As established by many classic Peanuts comics, Snoopy is the world's most self-assured beagle. He is Joe Cool after all. But Charlie Brown's little dog doesn't need his sunglasses to be confident. When it comes to his crush on Lucy, he shows how he feels. There are so many comics of Snoopy giving the girl an innocent smooch, only for her to be grossed out that she was kissed by a dog.

In this strip, Lucy visits Snoopy on Halloween night and asks for a trick or treat. Not having any candy in his doghouse, Snoopy gives her a kiss instead before going back to staring at the stars as Lucy stands there in disbelief. What a dog.

6
"A Pumpkin With Ticklish Ears"

Snoopy is capable of being around Lucy without letting his feelings get in the way. He's often seen hanging around the friend of his boy owner, and in this strip he watches dutifully as Lucy carves a pumpkin into a Jack-o'-lantern. More like a regular dog here than one with human characteristics, as soon as the pumpkin is done and Lucy walks away, he immediately jumps in headfirst.

If you've ever had a dog, you know they'll do hilarious things like this for whatever reason. Now, with Snoopy's ears sticking out (he must be looking out through the eyeholes), Linus walks up and gives the ears a scratch. There's no kid in Peanuts who will believe in anything as Linus does. If he is so certain that there's a Great Pumpkin, why can't a Jack-o'-lantern have dog ears too?

5
"Marcie Has Heard About Linus and the Great Pumpkins"
https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress%2Fwp-content%2Fauthors%2F67464712ef012-shawn-van-horn-white-background%281%29.png?fit=crop&w=90&h=90

Peanuts becomes so much about Linus when it's Halloween season (as proven by the best Peanuts specials). The boy is the philosopher of the group, the one whose mind is constantly wondering about the mysteries of the universe, even if he's too young to understand any of it. When October hits, he becomes solely focused on being visited by the Great Pumpkin in the local pumpkin patch.

Linus will tell anyone who will listen about the Great Pumpkin, including Marcie. She listens silently to his bizarre fantasies, takes it all in, and as only the mild-mannered Marcie can do, lets her friend know that his reputation precedes him.

4
"Snoopy Needs a Night Light Too After a Scary Movie"

Long before kids were being scared by more intense and gory modern horror movies, past generations needed only old-school monsters to be terrified. Then, it was about the lingering thoughts and an imagination out of control that brought the fear.

In this strip, Charlie Brown, Snoopy, and Linus watch a Frankenstein movie together. As Charlie Brown leaves Linus's house, they're thankful to have night lights to help them through the dark night to come. The next two panels show the two friends sound asleep at peace because of their night lights. In the last panel, we see that Snoopy has one too. Where's he plugging that lamp in, though?
